findings.claim: Requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. The collector never reads [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[DataContract] on T; it always uses contractless mode or the surrogate. The ledger answer for this (L19) is 'follow the requirement', so this acceptance criterion is unmet.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test: a formatter for a type annotated with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] in a referenced assembly. Assert the serialized bytes are an array (0x92). The current code emits a string-key map, so the test fails.

findings.claim: The ledger (L20) accepts name-sorted, read-write-only members, and the README documents that read-only members are skipped. This deviates from ContractlessStandardResolver, which uses declaration order and includes get-only members. This is deliberate, so it is not a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L20] Name-sorted read-write-only is acceptable; [L18] contractless by default with an optional surrogate.

findings.claim: The new GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute has no [Conditional("NEVERDEFINED")] marker, unlike other attributes that only the generator or analyzer consumes. The ledger says those are marked on purpose. Whether this attribute should follow that convention is unclear. [L14] covers only the omission case, so there is no ledger entry deciding it here.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the other generator-only attributes in Attributes.cs with the new GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute. Cite [L14]: attributes consumed only by the analyzer or generator are marked [Conditional("NEVERDEFINED")].

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements contractless mode by default plus an optional SurrogateType. It ignores any MessagePack attributes on T. No attribute-copy or attribute-generation approach is used.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: The generator honours the MessagePack attributes on T when they are present, and falls back to contractless only when there are none. It also supports DataContract/DataMember, so there is no need for a surrogate to carry keys.
